answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns: four seasons with three ordinary rounds each. Courtship rounds (4, 8, 12, 16) have no player turns; resolve only courtship, with no service rotation, Servants’ Hall use, or monument income.
answers.evidence: Overview: “each player takes twelve ordinary turns”; courtship has “no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.”

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate servants (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve the round-track event; resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; choose an activity tile; invite exactly the required gentry; provide required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy one tile; cleanup. At cleanup, used servants go to Expended Service, gentry to the personal discard pile, and the activity tile returns to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. The last player advances the round marker.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity: numbered steps 1–8; “all servants used…go to Expended Service; all played gentry…to your personal discard pile.”

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available Service; recover all gentry in your discard to hand; resolve round-track event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free full Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Hiring through Butler’s Room is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: “all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.”

answers.answer: Yes. Reputation is screened at the end of step 2, before choosing the activity, so 6.1 qualifies the PR6 tile and guests for this activity even if four Service Help actions later lower actual reputation to 3.4. Service Help moves a servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one from Expended Service. The step-2 reputation is the screening value for the whole activity.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening: “fixed at the end of step 2, before Choose Activity” and “remains the screening level for the whole activity”; Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; within either group their order is your choice. At minimum reputation you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to shelter its loss; losses stop at 1.1. A guest with a money penalty can be played only if the penalty is fully payable, using positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money if needed; otherwise you cannot play it.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6 and money penalty rule: “positive favours before all negative favours”; “A money penalty must be fully payable.”

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gains £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments for a full refresh; special-action refresh is once per turn. At minimum reputation you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table: costs/effects/limits; “At minimum you cannot…take a special action”; Service Help cannot take directly from Expended Service.

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no fee. On first use the tile upgrades. The upgraded room may instead recruit one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; it cannot recruit a unique servant.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Butler’s Room paragraph.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, or footman) even when that type is still available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution rules.

answers.answer: The Butler’s Pantry is the only way to acquire an underbutler: purchase it and take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. It is not immediately available; normally it moves to Quarters at your next service rotation and to Available Service at your second subsequent rotation, though passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available sooner. Once in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Butler’s Pantry paragraph.

answers.answer: In the Market, price is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed modifier. In Reserve, the base price is £300 plus the modifier. Minimum price is £100. You may never acquire a duplicate of a tile you already own, but reputation does not restrict buying above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: “market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier”; Reserve base £300; minimum £100; no duplicate; reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space becomes empty, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. Stack a drawn duplicate on its matching Market tile and draw again; if multiple spaces are being filled, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. A Reserve-eligible tile goes directly to Reserve and another is drawn. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so it does not trigger refill.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve, Refill paragraph.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles to Reserve except Largest Wine Cellar; later Service draws also go directly there, with that exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and route later PR1 draws there too. A full seasonal Market refresh is standard: after each of the first three courtships, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve paragraph; full refresh occurs after “each of the first three courtships.”

answers.answer: At ordinary courtship, return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall first. Score the current face-up theme, counting only the currently face-up hybrid category and including negative tile VP. Highest score wins one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. If tied, each tied player draws a VP card and no Fairchild is awarded. Every player discards one objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them on the bottom of the objective deck. After courtships 1–3 the first-player marker passes anticlockwise.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep: ordinary courtship scoring, tie, objective discard, and upkeep order.

answers.answer: Final courtship scores tile VP across all four revealed themes, counting a repeated category twice, including negative VP. Highest score gets one VP card and a Fairchild; a tie is broken by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position. If still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective, then players get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible before scoring.
answers.evidence: Final courtship paragraph.

answers.answer: End-game categories: improvement tiles (all face-up VP, including negatives); gentry in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild; dismissed guests excluded); fulfilled objectives; reputation; servants (2 VP each); wealth (1 VP per £200, rounded down); retained unused VP cards (printed VP). Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP. Ties: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise higher reputation level wins; if still tied, share victory.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and tie paragraph.

answers.answer: Normally you receive five objectives at setup plus two on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase the retained total and do not add a discard. Put discards face down at the bottom of the objective deck; shuffle simultaneous discards together first. Named-tile objectives require owning the tiles at game end, not upgraded sides.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards paragraph.

answers.answer: A VP card benefit may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (multiple cards may be used), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards score their printed VP at game end; you cannot take both benefit and VP from one card.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: VP card use and disposition paragraph.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile remains upgraded on later uses. Hybrids start with the underlined category showing, flip after every use, and move to the newly face-up category. A Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite upgrades after its one activity use into an ongoing monument and can never host again; its ongoing benefit starts on later turns. For courtship and objectives, only a hybrid’s currently face-up category counts.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal tiles, hybrids, monuments.

answers.answer: Monuments pay one reputation during the ongoing-effects step on each ordinary turn, hosting or passing, but not during courtship; a newly purchased monument starts paying on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works during step 2 when hosting and step 3 when passing: place one available servant there to lower one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; the servant goes to Expended Service and cannot also serve the activity. It cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Monuments and Servants’ Hall paragraphs.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: put one footman on the tile, play one casual guest from hand and provide that guest’s normal service; double all guest favours, including negative ones; it upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile, one prestige guest from hand with normal service; double one chosen favour and resolve the others normally; upgrades to a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draw one prestige guest to attend without personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, not negative ones; keep guest and put it in discard at cleanup; upgrades to a monument. Each suite has a fixed count of one guest; no effect changes it.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and fixed count statement.

answers.answer: Randomly choose the first player. Starting with the player to that player’s left and proceeding clockwise, players choose an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith adds a Dowager Countess; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Each player starts at reputation level 1, position 1; use the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. Each receives a butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid, and footman in Available Service; five starting tiles (Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green) with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady family cards. Ponsonby is the only family that starts with money (£300).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3, and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, put 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen, and 2 underbutlers in Servants for Hire. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked there. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for the game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: per-player counts, two underbutlers total, no butlers/housekeepers, unused servants unavailable.

answers.answer: Shuffle starter guests separately from the casual deck and deal two to each player’s hand; shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise use normal casual rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry paragraph on starter guests.

answers.answer: For four players, select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). You may select at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against this selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Opening Market: draw until six different eligible tiles fill its spaces; eligible means PR3 or less (including no PR), not Servants’ Hall, and not a double-sided monument. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack duplicate eligible tiles in the same space. Normal tiles start with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort the six spaces by ascending sorting number beginning at £300. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are excluded.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Set Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme face up and keep revealed themes in order through the game. Put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild cards face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is not hidden; old revealed themes remain in play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; themes are kept in order through the game.

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, the servant in Expended Service moves to Servants’ Quarters, while the servant already in Quarters moves to Available Service. An available servant you do not use remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: each advances exactly one space; unused available servants remain available.

answers.answer: No. The Village Fair event checks whether Private Study is already upgraded at that step; upgrading it later that same turn does not grant the reward immediately. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Private Study paragraph: upgraded side reward on Village Fair rounds only.

answers.answer: Round 6’s Draw Objectives event is resolved on each player’s turn after service rotation and before ongoing effects/activity choice (or during the event step on a pass). Draw two objectives and keep both secret with the others. Passing players also resolve the event because round events apply on each player’s turn.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 2 checks the round event; Passing resolves event; standard event table says draw two and keep both.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday ignores PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so lower-reputation players may play higher-PR tiles and guests. All other requirements still apply, including service and exact gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track events: National Holiday; hosting step 4–5.

answers.answer: Yes, Builders’ Holiday allows any number of Market and/or Reserve purchases within funds. Finish all purchases before sliding/refilling; use the unchanged Market and the prices (space or Reserve base plus printed modifier) that applied before the sequence. Do not refresh between purchases with a special action or VP card. Market Purchase VP-card benefits use the same Builders’ Holiday rules and restrictions.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all removed Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; refill all six spaces under normal rules, then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix them in, so they cannot reappear during that refresh. Reserve tiles stay in Reserve unchanged.
answers.evidence: Refresh paragraph: set all Market tiles aside, leave Reserve unchanged, refill, then return tiles to bag.

answers.answer: Reputation symbols are increments: clockwise gains and anticlockwise losses; crossing 5 to 1 raises a level, and 1 to 5 lowers a level. Standard minimum is 1.1; maximum is 7.5 (Max.5), with losses beyond minimum ignored. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; you can spend it before or during resolving a reputation favour to make room.
answers.evidence: Reputation section: increment arithmetic, minimum/maximum, losses, and Max.5 handling.

answers.answer: Money held is public. Players may not give or receive money between them. You may never spend more than you hold. The common money supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Money held is public; no transfers; never spend more than you have; supply unlimited.

answers.answer: For a “ladies” requirement, female family members or female guests can fill it; for “gentlemen,” male family members or male guests can fill it. A casual-guest requirement requires casual guests and excludes family. You must meet the exact printed number and types, with no extras or shortfall. Family members need no personal service and have no PR.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 4: ladies/gentlemen definitions, casual/prestige vs family requirements, exact count; family has no PR and no personal service.

answers.answer: For an ordinary guest invite, reveal the drawn guest to everyone and add it to hand. For screening, draw the stated number and choose the stated number to keep; reveal only the kept cards and add them to hand. Put rejected screened cards on the bottom of their guest deck without revealing them.
answers.evidence: Enjoy Favours: new invites revealed to everyone; Gentry screening paragraph.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so you need not dismiss anyone if you have no unwanted guests. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, the current activity, or discard, including one drawn earlier by a favour. Family cannot be dismissed. A dismissed guest goes to the bottom of its matching deck, is no longer yours, will not return on passing, and does not score.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: dismissal paragraph.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose either screening two casual guests and keeping one, or optionally dismissing one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation.
answers.evidence: Base family card table and Asquith Dowager statement.

answers.answer: The Young Lady gets the admirer bonus only if a male prestige guest attends the same activity. A male casual guest does not qualify; a female prestige guest does not qualify; Charles Fairchild does qualify because he is a male prestige guest. The bonus is two reputation. She still draws one casual guest in each case.
answers.evidence: Base family card table: draws one casual guest and gains two reputation if a male prestige guest attends; Charles is male and prestige.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR; he requires a valet and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR; she requires a lady’s maid and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are prestige guests, not family cards, so family dismissal immunity does not apply to them.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: Charles male/Elizabeth female, both prestige with no PR; services/favours; family can never be dismissed.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: base gossips and minimum-reputation protection.

answers.answer: The Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing gives no reputation.
answers.evidence: Barn paragraph.

answers.answer: The Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant from the Servants’ Quarters area on each turn, in addition to Available Service; it is a tile ability, separate from Service Help and ordinary rotation. The servant used goes to Expended Service normally. Service Help instead moves a servant from Quarters to Available Service. The tile can supply one Quarters servant per turn.
answers.evidence: Servants’ Quarters tile paragraph; Service Help action.

answers.answer: Private Study’s front side requires two family members and a butler, and has no tile favour. It upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile. Its upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds only; you do not host it again to receive this, so it cannot be repeatedly hosted for that income.
answers.evidence: Private Study paragraph.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library: butler and two family; draw one extra objective. Upgraded: butler and three family; draw one VP card. The extra objective increases the number retained for final scoring; it does not create an additional courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Main Library paragraph; objectives section on additional objectives.

answers.answer: The Objective VP card draws two objectives, keeps one, and returns the other to the bottom of the objective deck. It grants one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service and they can be used immediately, including servants from Expended Service. Service Help only moves one servant from Quarters to Available Service and cannot take one directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Refresh Service; Service Help rule.

answers.answer: A Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire into Expended Service; underbutlers are excluded. It cannot immediately provide service from Expended Service; it must advance through the normal rotation unless another stated effect moves it.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Hire Servant; service rotation.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest may return a family member from your personal discard pile to your hand. If returned before Invite Gentry, you may choose that card to attend the current activity if it meets the requirements; returning it does not automatically play it.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Refresh Guest.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids, excluding butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary servant end-game VP counts every servant type and location at 2 VP each. The ten-servant objective counts at least ten servants total, without the basic-servant restriction.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: basic-servant definition; Final VP servants; objective row for ten servants.

answers.answer: The upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count as monuments for the monument objective. For category objectives, only a tile’s current category counts; for hybrids, the currently face-up category counts, so each counts in one category at a time.
answers.evidence: Monuments paragraph; hybrid category rule; base objective reference: category bonuses and monuments.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus any one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. The named tiles need only be owned at game end; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference rows; tile objective rule says ownership, not upgrading.

answers.answer: The prestige-guest bonus scores 1 VP per prestige guest; the every-three-guests bonus scores 1 VP per complete set of three nonfamily guests, so incomplete groups earn nothing. A final Fairchild counts as a prestige guest and as a nonfamily guest for these objectives.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: guest bonuses; prestige guests include a final Fairchild.

answers.answer: The reputation objective awards 7 VP for reaching maximum level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective awards 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP depends on level only (levels 1–7 score 1/3/6/10/15/21/28); wheel position does not affect it or reputation tie resolution.
answers.evidence: Objective reference: reputation and wealth; Final VP and tie rules.

answers.answer: West Terrace remains an activity on both sides. Both sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. Unupgraded: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded: draw one prestige guest and may dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of their decks. It never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements section: West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no hand or discard-pile limit. Gentry in your discard pile still belong to you and score normally at game end.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: “There is no hand or discard-pile limit”; discard-pile gentry score normally.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including one underneath another in a stack; there is no top-tile-only rule. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve paragraph.

answers.answer: You may choose to pass even when you could host. If you cannot meet an activity’s required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 5; turn structure says choose host or pass.

answers.answer: Yes. On a passing turn you may combine the free passing-benefit Market refresh, one paid special-action Market refresh, and multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each providing its own full refresh. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action refresh; pass and VP-card refreshes do not use it. This combination is subject to purchase-timing restrictions, including no refreshing between purchases in a Builders’ Holiday or Market Purchase buying sequence.
answers.evidence: Special actions: other refresh methods do not use the once-per-turn allowance; multiple Market Refresh VP cards and combination with pass/special refresh; buying restrictions paragraph.
